findings.detail: All three newly-closed rows have byte-identical `Fixed by` cells describing the `alignBatchResults` numeric-translation fix — which is TD-042's fix only. TD-039 was actually fixed by adding the `'no-model'` state to `ApiKeyStatus`, `verifyGeminiKey` and the modal badge; TD-041 by `advancePastRetiredModel` plus the `onNotice` threading. Separately, TD-039's Description cell now ends mid-sentence at ``returns `'valid' \`` — the `\|` escapes from the original open-table row were not preserved when the row moved, so the first unescaped `|` terminated the cell and swallowed the rest of the description. The register is a living document whose entire value is being an accurate record; as it stands, anyone who reads why TD-039 or TD-041 was closed is told about a different change entirely, and the two commits in this PR are no longer recoverable from it. Docs-only, no runtime impact, which is why this is not higher.
findings.summary: Closed rows for TD-039 and TD-041 carry TD-042's fix text; TD-039's description is truncated

findings.detail: The `no-model` badge (line 93) and the help panel (lines 108-112) are rendered conditionally after the async `handleTestGemini` resolves, with no `role="status"`, `role="alert"` or `aria-live` on either. A screen-reader user who presses Test hears nothing when the result arrives, and this is the one status whose whole purpose is to redirect the user away from the wrong conclusion ("my key is bad") — the badge text alone does that work, and it is never announced. The existing `valid`/`invalid`/`quota` badges have the same gap, so this is not a regression and the diff only adds one more instance, which is why it is `low` rather than `medium`.
findings.summary: New 'no-model' badge and help panel appear with no live region

findings.detail: The test drives `generateText` directly with a callback, so it proves the service-layer plumbing works — but the only `generateText` call site in the app is `components/SupportChat.tsx:448`, `aiService.generateText(prompt, 'fast')`, with no third argument. Support Chat is therefore still the one feature where a model fallback is invisible, which is precisely the condition TD-041 describes and which this PR's commit message ("report a fallback everywhere") and the register's closure of TD-041 both claim is now gone. The test name asserts a caller relationship that does not exist, so the suite will stay green if the gap is never closed. Impact is genuinely small — Support Chat is conversational and its answers are read immediately — which is why this is `low`. It would be `medium` if Support Chat output were exported or persisted the way Translate's workbook is.
findings.summary: Test named "generateText tells its caller — Support Chat" but no caller passes onNotice

findings.detail: The new file header states the reason `ModelNotice` is imported rather than redeclared: "a second local copy would let this file and the interface drift — which is the same mistake as the three separate copies of `translateBatch`'s options shape." But `translateBatch`'s own `options.onNotice` is still spelled `(message: string) => void` inline, with its own 5-line doc comment duplicating the one now on `ModelNotice` in `types/ai.types.ts` — while the corresponding field in `IAiService` was converted to `ModelNotice`. The two are structurally identical so nothing breaks today; the cost is that the one function the PR is holding up as the cautionary example is the one place the new type was not applied, and the duplicated prose is a second thing to keep in sync.
findings.summary: translateBatch's options still declares an inline copy of ModelNotice
